brief: The viewer sees a massive, dark, and fragile architectural structure built from glass prisms, viewed at eye-level. This ziggurat is perpetually unstable, appearing to continuously cascade and slide downward in a steady, geometric collapse. The colors are dark, reflecting the fragility of the glass. Although the structure has constant, natural motion, the system is reactive: clicking anywhere on the canvas causes the megalith to peel off and shed additional segments, accelerating the downward cascade.

statement: This sketch presents an architectural marvel constructed from glass prisms that exists in a perpetual state of instability. The structure appears to cascade and slide downward in a continuous geometric collapse, rendered in dark tones that emphasize the fragility of the glass. The viewer experiences both natural motion and a responsive element: clicking anywhere on the canvas triggers a cascade effect where segments peel off and accelerate their descent. The piece combines physics-based animation with interactive feedback to create an immersive visualization of an architectural structure that is both beautiful and inherently unstable, where each click becomes a catalyst for the ongoing collapse.
